subject: Climate & Environment
title: Carbon Dioxide: The Main Driver
description: A fast breakdown of Carbon Dioxide: The Main Driver for builders.

hook.text: CO₂ makes up less than 0.04% of the atmosphere. Yet it controls Earth's thermostat.

buildup.text: Every carbon atom in coal, oil, and gas was buried underground for millions of years.

discovery.text: Burning fossil fuels releases that stored carbon back into the air as CO₂.

twist.text: CO₂ levels now top 420 ppm — higher than any point in 800,000 years.

climax.text: Each molecule lingers for centuries, trapping heat long after the fire goes out.

punchline.text: A tiny fraction of the air is rewriting Earth's future.

quiz.question: How long can a CO₂ molecule remain in the atmosphere?

details.summary: Carbon dioxide is the most important human-emitted greenhouse gas, now at over 420 parts per million, the highest level in at least 800,000 years. It persists in the atmosphere for centuries, making every ton emitted a virtually permanent addition to the warming total.
details.whyItMatters: CO2's long atmospheric lifetime means emissions accumulate over decades. This is why net-zero targets exist: only stopping emissions entirely can stabilize CO2 levels.
takeaways: CO2 has risen from 280 ppm pre-industrial to over 420 ppm today
It persists in the atmosphere for hundreds to thousands of years
Fossil fuel burning and deforestation are the main human sources

faq.question: How do we know current CO2 levels are unprecedented?
faq.answer: Ice cores from Antarctica trap ancient air bubbles stretching back 800,000 years. They show CO2 never exceeded 300 ppm during that period. Today's 420 ppm is roughly 50 percent higher than any level in the ice-core record.

faq.question: Will CO2 levels drop if we stop emitting today?
faq.answer: CO2 would very slowly decline over centuries as oceans and vegetation absorb the excess, but much would remain for thousands of years. This is why every fraction of a degree of warming we avoid matters permanently.
